description:
Follow-up from bd-pl2 / GH#21, point 1 of the reporter's ask, only PARTLY met.

The new warning names the comparands as "the newest write stamp bn has seen for
this store" — a label chosen because it is true of ALL FOUR call sites. But the
four are genuinely different references:

  daemon/runtime/core/repo_load.rs:264  -> max stamp across every bead loaded
                                           from the git repo
  daemon/runtime/coord/sync.rs:165,:323 -> RUNNING max for the store
                                           (max_write_stamp; never decreases)
  daemon/runtime/core/repl_ingest.rs:261 -> newest stamp in the batch that just
                                           arrived (plain assign — CAN decrease)
  daemon/runtime/executor.rs:461        -> the stamp of the write this daemon
                                           just made (local HLC post-tick)

Telling the user which one produced the figure would let them distinguish "my
clock vs my own repo" from "my clock vs whatever a peer just sent me" — quite
different diagnoses.

Blocked on a change OUTSIDE the fixing agent's allowed paths, which is why it
was not done: add a `source: ClockSkewSource` field to `SyncWarning::ClockSkew`
in crates/kopi-beans/src/api/issues.rs:32-35. Once that exists the daemon side is
a one-line wire-through each at query_executor.rs:803 and git_lane.rs:45, and the
renderer in cli_surface/commands/status.rs just prints it.

NOTE while you are in there: `WriteStamp` carries NO actor attribution — only
`Stamp` has `by` (core/time.rs:130-134), and `max_write_stamp()` throws it away
(core/state/canonical.rs:621-630). So the reporter's suggested "actor <id>'s last
write" phrasing CANNOT be honoured without either plumbing `by` through or
inventing a fact. Don't invent lah.
title: kopi-beans: SyncWarning::ClockSkew has no source field — cannot say WHICH reference stamp it compared
